guarantees.claim: txcnt_eq_blksz is initialized to '0, and if digest_size_i does not match SHA2_256, SHA2_384, or SHA2_512, the output remains '0.
When digest_size_i equals SHA2_256, txcnt_eq_blksz asserts iff the lower BlockSizeBitsSHA256 bits of txcount are zero and txcount is not all-zero.
When digest_size_i equals SHA2_384, txcnt_eq_blksz asserts iff the lower BlockSizeBitsSHA512 bits of txcount are zero and txcount is not all-zero.
When digest_size_i equals SHA2_512, txcnt_eq_blksz asserts iff the lower BlockSizeBitsSHA512 bits of txcount are zero and txcount is not all-zero.

assumptions.claim: digest_size_i is always one of the legal enumerated values SHA2_256, SHA2_384, or SHA2_512.
assumptions.risk: If an illegal or glitched value appears, default fallback forces txcnt_eq_blksz to '0, preventing detection of block-size-aligned txcount; this may hang or mis-sequence the HMAC data path.

uncertain_points.claim: The case statement only handles SHA2_256, SHA2_384, SHA2_512; other possible legal digest_size_i values (e.g., SHAKE variants or future codes) are silently mapped to txcnt_eq_blksz=0.
uncertain_points.cond: digest_size_i takes a supported but uncovered value
uncertain_points.risk: Incorrect block-boundary detection, leading to HMAC processing errors or stalls when new algorithm support is added without updating this block.
